p: The Greek manuscript G turns the words around: 'the Lord of the flesh'.

t: 'Beyond the overseer' or 'except to the overseer'?
p: The long recension reads 'except' (plēn) for 'more than' (pleon); the Syriac also has 'except'.

Lightfoot: 'There is no sufficient reason however for displacing the reading πλέον here', and it should 'still probably be interpreted in the same way'; 'The Oriental versions must either have had πλήν, or must have interpreted πλέον in this way.' Lake's English gives that sense: 'if it be made known except to the bishop'.

p: The long recension and the Syriac and Armenian read 'with God'; Lightfoot prints it.

p: Lake's footnote: the long recension and the Armenian read 'through your intercession'.

why: The Plain English Translation follows Lake, who renders 'your disciple at the resurrection' and adds 'Or perhaps "a disciple at your resurrection."' Lightfoot prefers 'through your intercession' because of the parallel in Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans 11:1 ('so that through your prayer I may reach God') and the agreement of the long recension with the Armenian; he grants that 'the other reading ... would make very good sense', setting suffering against resurrection as in Ignatius to the Romans 4:3.
